reflection_text.2:
The model is the cross $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ in ${\mathbb R}^{d}$ and the random set $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.

* Volume.  With $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $U_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$, $K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d. and $|U|\sim U[0,1]$,
${\mathbb E}|U|=1/2$.  On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;a\;perm.}\}$
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K{\rm \;perm.}\}=d!/d^{d}$.  Hence

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=d!^{-1}{\mathbb E}|\det|=(2d)^{-d}$,
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}^{0}=2^{-d}/d!$ on the one-point-per-axis
normalisation.  ${\mathbb E}|X_{i}|=1/2$.

* Pairwise distance.  $E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and
$$
I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$
For $i\neq j$
${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=d^{-1}2/3+(d-1)d^{-1}I$.
The mean unordered pair distance of $S_{d}$ is therefore
$$
\bar D_{d}= \frac{d{\mathbb E}|X|+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
               {\binom{d+1}{2}}
        =\frac{\, (5d-2)/3+I(d-1)^{2}\,}{d(d+1)}
        =\frac{1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{d+1},
$$
with $\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  On the one-point-per-axis convention
$\bar D_{d}^{0}=\bigl[1+(d-1)I\bigr]/(d+1)$.

Hence for the i.i.d. cross model
$$
R_{d}^{\rm iid}= \frac{(2d)^{-d}}{\bar D_{d}}
 =\frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{(5d-2)/3+I(d-1)^{2}},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$
$R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$, $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$, etc.  The series is super-exponential,
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm iid}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117$,
about $1.117$–$1.118$ to three figures, essentially $1.117$.

On the usual one-point-per-axis, i.e. $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{i}$,
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}^{0}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{0}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$, so that
$$
R_{d}^{0}= \frac{(d+1)2^{-d}}{d!\,[1+(d-1)I]},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$
$R_{2}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}\approx0.03293$, $R_{4}\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$,
etc., and
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{0}\approx1.000+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038\approx1.250$,
$1.2497$ unrounded.  This is the $1.25$ value quoted by the
distinct-axes camp.

The point-point normalisation ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}^{0}/I$ gives
$\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/(d!I)=(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$, the $0.848$ remark
often quoted.

The remaining disagreement is therefore the distinct-axes vs i.i.d.-cross
interpretation and whether the denominator is the mean over all
$\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs including the origin or the $X\!-\!X$ mean only.
Under the literal i.i.d. sampling from the cross with the pairwise mean
over $S_{d}$ the sum is $\approx1.117$, the conventional one-per-axis
normalisation giving the familiar $\approx1.250$.
reflection_text.10:
The discussion is dominated by two modelling choices for the d points on the d-orthogonal cross.

*Cross i.i.d. model.*  Put $X_i=T_i e_{K_i}$ with $T_i\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d.  Then
${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$, $P\{K_1,\dots ,K_d {\rm perm.}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and
$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_d=\frac{{\mathbb E}|\det[X_1\dots X_d]|}{d!}
     =\frac{(1/2)^d}{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_1=1/2 .
$$
For $i\ne j$
$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|
   =\frac1d\,{\mathbb E}|T_i-T_j|+\frac{d-1}{d}\,
     {\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_i^2+T_j^2}
   =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I}{d},
$$
with 
$$
I={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_1^2+T_2^2}
   =\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1\sqrt{u^2+v^2}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$
For the $d+1$ set $\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\}$ the unordered-pair mean is
$$
\bar D_d=\frac{d{\mathbb E}|X_i|+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|}{\binom{d+1}2}
       =\frac{1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|}{d+1}
       =\frac{d+(d-1)2/3+(d-1)^2I}{d(d+1)} .
$$
Hence with the origin-averaged distance
$$
R_d^{\rm iid}= \frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_d}{\bar D_d}
 =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|}
 =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}d}{d+(d-1)2/3+(d-1)^2I},
$$
$R_1=1$ and
$R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_5\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$, etc.  The series is super-exponential,
$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm iid}\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
\approx1.117$,
about $1.117\!-\!1.118$ to three figures.  With the point-point
normalisation $R_d^{\rm iid,pp}=(2d)^{-d}/{\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|$ the
$d\ge2$ tail is $\approx0.094$.

*Distinct-axis model.*  If the $d$ points are forced to lie one per
axis, $X_i=T_i e_i$, then
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$ and with the same $I$
$$
\bar D_d^{\rm dist}= \frac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1},
\qquad
R_d^{\rm dist}= \frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
$$
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.212$, $R_3\approx0.0329$, $R_4\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$
and $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm dist}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
The point-point version is ${\mathbb R}_n=2^{-n}/(n!\,I)$ with sum
$(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$.

The wording “independent stochastic points … uniform on the union of
the $d$ orthogonal segments” points to the i.i.d. cross model, i.e.
$E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$ and the origin-included average pairwise
distance $\bar D_d$ above.  The $1.25$ value is the familiar
one-point-per-axis normalisation $2^{-d}/d!$ with $\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$,
the source of the $1.250$ quotes.  The unresolved modelling ambiguity is
whether $K_i$ are i.i.d. uniform on $\{1..d\}$ or a fixed permutation,
and whether the denominator is the full $d+1$ unordered-pair mean
$\bar D_d$ or the pure point-point mean ${\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|$.  Under
the i.i.d. cross with origin-included average the series is essentially
$1.000+0.109+0.008+0.0004+\dots$, i.e. $\approx1.117$ to three decimals.

reflection_text.11:
The problem is about a d-dimensional cross
$C_d=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_k$ and the random set $S_d=\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\}$,
$X_i=U_i e_{K_i}$ i.i.d., $U_i\sim{\rm Unif}[-1,1]$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$.
Two modelling choices are in circulation.

*Distinct-axis / permutation model* $K_i$ are a permutation.
Then $|\det[X_1\ldots X_d]|=\prod|U_i|$ a.s. and
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$.
With $S={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^2+V^2}= (\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.765196$
the mean unordered pair distance of $\{0,X_i\}$ is
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1)$.
Hence $R_d^{\rm perm}= (d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl[d!\,(1+(d-1)S)\bigr]$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.212$, $R_3\approx0.0329$, $R_4\approx0.00395$,
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm perm}\approx1.2497\approx1.25$.
This is the $1.25$ value repeatedly quoted by Colleagues 1,2,4,11.

*I.i.d. cross model* the $K_i$ are i.i.d. The volume is non-zero only on
$\{K_1,\ldots ,K_d{\rm \;perm.}\}$ with probability $d!/d^{d}$.
$ {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_d=( {\mathbb E}|U|)^{d}d!/d^{d}/d!=(2d)^{-d}$,
${\mathbb E}|U|=1/2$, ${\mathbb E}|U-V|=2/3$.
For $i\neq j$
${\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|=d^{-1}2/3+(d-1)d^{-1}S=:E_d$.
The mean unordered pair distance of $S_d$ is
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)E_d]/(d+1)$.
Thus
$R_d =\dfrac{(2d)^{-d}(d+1)}{1+(d-1)E_d}
     =\dfrac{(2d)^{-d}(d+1)}{1+(d-1)\Bigl[\dfrac{2}{3d}+\dfrac{d-1}{d}S\Bigr]}$,
$R_1=1$.

Numerically with $S=(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.7651957$,
$R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00752$, $R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_5\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$, tail $O((2d)^{-d})$.
Hence
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d =1+0.10927+0.00752+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117\approx1.1172$,
about $1.12$ to the quoted three figures.  Discarding the trivial $d=1$
term the non-trivial tail is $\approx0.117$.

The $1.250$ value is the permutation / one-point-per-arm normalisation
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$ with the same $\bar D_d$, i.e. the
conventional “origin included’’ average used in Colleagues 1,2,4,11.
The i.i.d. formulation is the one consistent with “independent stochastic
points’’ on the union of the $d$ orthogonal segments.  The series is
super-exponentially convergent, essentially $1+R_2+R_3$.

Unresolved / sensitivity: the exact value of the mean inter-point distance
$S=\int_0^1\!\int_0^1\sqrt{u^2+v^2}du\,dv$ is
$S=(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.765196$; numerical quadrature shifts
the third decimal only in the $10^{-4}$ range.  The point-point only
normalisation ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_d/{\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|$ gives a
different constant $\approx1.094$ with the $d=1$ term retained.
reflection_text.12:
The discussion splits on two modelling choices and on how the pairwise distance is normalised.

* One-point-per-axis convention.  Put $X_i=Y_i e_i$, $Y_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.  Then 
${\rm Vol}_d={\prod_i|Y_i|}/d!$, $E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$, $E|X_i|=1/2$ and for $i\ne j$
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{Y_1^2+Y_2^2}=J$ with
$J=\int_0^1\!\int_0^1\!\sqrt{u^2+v^2}du dv
 =[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)]/3\approx0.765196$.
For the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_i\}$ the mean unordered pair distance is
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)J]/(d+1)$ and
$R_d=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)2^{-d}/\big[d!\,\big(1+(d-1)J\big)\big]$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.2124$, $R_3\approx0.0329$, $R_4\approx0.00395$.
Hence $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1.000+0.212+0.033+0.004+\dots\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
This is the $1.25$ value quoted by Colleagues 1,2,4,7,11.

* Fully i.i.d. axis choice.  Write $X_i=T_i e_{K_i}$ with $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\dots d\}$ i.i.d. and
$T_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.  Then ${\mathbb P}\{K_1,\dots ,K_d$ is a permutation$\}=d!/d^{\,d}$ and
$E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$.  For $i\ne j$
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=d^{-1}E|T_i-T_j|+(d-1)d^{-1}J$, $E|T_i-T_j|=2/3$, so
$E_{d}= [2/3+(d-1)J]/d$ and the mean distance of a random unordered pair of the
$d+1$ point set $\{0,X_i\}$ is
$D_d=[1+(d-1)E_d]/(d+1)=[\,(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^2J\,]/[d(d+1)]$.
With $R_d^{iid}=E{\rm Vol}_d/D_d$,
$R_d^{iid}=(d+1)/\big[2^{d}d^{\,d-1}\big((5d-2)/3+(d-1)^2J\big)\big]$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.1093$, $R_3\approx0.0075$, $R_4\approx3.8\times10^{-4}$,
and $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{iid}\approx1+0.1093+0.0075+0.00038+\dots\approx1.117$,
about $1.117\!-\!1.118$.  This is the i.i.d. average-pair value repeatedly quoted
by Colleagues 10,12,5,6,8.

The point–point normalisation $E{\rm Vol}_d/E\|X_i-X_j\|$ gives the closed form
$(e^{1/2}-1)/J\approx0.848$ in the one-point-per-axis convention, and
$R_d^{pp}=(2d)^{-d}/E_d$ in the i.i.d. convention with a $\approx0.094$ non-trivial tail.

The wording “independent stochastic points’’ favours the i.i.d. axis model and the
average over the $d+1$ points, i.e. the $\approx1.117$ sum, while the classic
one-point-per-axis simplex literature gives the often quoted $\approx1.250$
sum.  The $1.250$ value is the one-point-per-axis average-pair sum and the
$1.117$ value is the fully i.i.d. average-pair sum; the remaining
discrepancy is entirely the $d!/d^{\,d}$ permutation probability and the
choice of pairwise normalisation. ∎

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The wording is the key.  The candidate set is the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin in the unit ball and the ensemble that is added to $\{0\}$ contains exactly $d$ points and exactly $d$ distinct segments, the numbers matching.  That is a bijection points $\leftrightarrow$ lines, not an i.i.d. draw with replacement from the union.  Up to relabelling we may write

$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{i},\qquad U_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;i=1\ldots d$,

one point on each orthogonal arm.  On this model the $d$-simplex
$\operatorname{conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ is non-degenerate a.s. and

${\rm Vol}_{d}= \dfrac{|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]|}{d!}
             =\dfrac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|U_{i}|}{d!}$.

With $E|U|=1/2$

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \dfrac{(1/2)^{d}}{d!}=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad 
E|U|=1/2$,

the $d!/d^{d}$ factor that appears for sampling with replacement does not belong to the stated set-up, because replacement would allow two points on the same arm and would make the hull degenerate with positive probability, contrary to the “distinct mutually orthogonal… with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ requirement.

For two different arms

$\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\sqrt{U_{i}^{2}+U_{j}^{2}}$ and

$J:=E\sqrt{U_{i}^{2}+U_{j}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765196.$

Hence for the $d+1$ points $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$

$E d_{0i}=1/2,\qquad E d_{ij}=J,\;i\neq j$,

and the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of the set is

$\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 J}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)J}{d+1}$.

The dimension-wise ratio is therefore

$R_{d}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)2^{-d}}{d!\,[1+(d-1)J]},\qquad R_{1}=1$,

$R_{2}= \dfrac{3\cdot2^{-2}}{2(1+J)}\approx0.2126$,
$R_{3}= \dfrac{4\cdot2^{-3}}{6[1+2J]}\approx0.0329$,
$R_{4}\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$, $R_{5}\approx3.8\times10^{-4}$, …

The series is $O(2^{-d}/d!)$ and is essentially exhausted after $d=4$:

$S_{N}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =1+0.2126+0.0329+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497$,

i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.250$ to three decimals.  This is the $1\!:\!1$
line-point normalisation that follows directly from the stated distinct
arms interpretation and is the $1.250$ value obtained by Colleagues 1,2,
4 and 11 for the origin-included mean pairwise distance.  The
$(2d)^{-d}$ volume that appears in the with-replacement i.i.d. model is an
extra $d!/d^{d}$ permutation assumption not required by the text.

2.text:
For a $d$ point cross let $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ and $U_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d.
and put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  Put $|U|\sim U[0,1]$, 
${\mathbb E}|U|=1/2$ and

$$
I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt 2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx0.7651957 .
$$

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}\}$ a permutation, ${\mathbb P}\{K\ {\rm perm}\}
=d!/d^{d}$,

$$
\bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]\bigr|
   =\prod_{i=1}^{d}|U_{i}|\qquad{\rm on\ \,the\ \,permutation},
$$

so that with ${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}S_{d})=|\det|/d!$,

$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{({\mathbb E}|U|)^{d}}{d!}
   =\frac{1}{(2d)^{d}},\qquad {\mathbb E}|X_{i}|=\frac12 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|U_{1}-U_{2}|+\frac{d-1}{d}I
   =\frac{2}{3d}+\frac{d-1}{d}I ,
\qquad{\mathbb E}|U_{1}-U_{2}|=\frac23 .
$$

Hence for the $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{d}$

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\,{\mathbb E}|X_{i}|
       +\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
      {\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{\,{\rm d}+\,d(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
      {d(d+1)}
 =\frac{(5d-2)/3+I(d-1)^{2}}{d(d+1)} ,
$$

$\bar D_{1}=1/2$, and

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
            {(5d-2)/3+I(d-1)^{2}},\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

In closed form with $C=3I=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)$

$$
R_{d}=\frac{3(d+1)}
          {2^{d}d^{\,d-1}\!\left[\,5d-2+(d-1)^{2}C\right]},\qquad
R_{1}=1,
$$

i.e.

* $R_{1}=1.000000$,
* $R_{2}=0.10927\ldots$,
* $R_{3}=7.51\times10^{-3}\ldots$,
* $R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}\ldots$,
* $R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}\ldots$,

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Hence

$$
S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.117\;,
$$

$1.117\!-\!1.118$ in the usual numerical quadrature, $S_{\infty}\approx
1.1172$ unrounded.  In particular $R_{1}=1$ and the non-trivial tail
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$.

Remark.  With the conventional one–point–per–axis normalisation
$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{i}$, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}^{0}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{0}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$, so that

$$
R_{d}^{0}=\frac{(d+1)2^{-d}}{d!\,[1+(d-1)I]},\qquad
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{0}\approx1.000+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+\cdots\approx
1.250,
$$

the $1.250$ value normally quoted for the distinct-axes model.  The
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ point–point normalisation is
$(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$.

4.text:
For the cross

$$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}\subset{\mathbf R}^{d}$$

let

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},
\qquad T_{i}\sim {\rm U}[-1,1],$$

i.i.d.  Put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ and 
$V_{d}={\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}S_{d})$.  On 
$\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;is\;a\;permutation}\}$,
${\bf P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;perm.}\}=d!/d^{d}$,

$$|\det [X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i=1}^{d}|T_{i}| 
{\bf 1}_{\{K\;{\rm perm.}\}},\qquad 
V_{d}= \frac{|\det [X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!},$$

so that with $E|T|=1/2$

\begin{equation*}
E V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{(E|T|)^{d}}{d!}
       =\frac{1}{(2d)^{d}},\qquad E|X_{i}|=\frac12 ,
\end{equation*}
$EV_{1}=1/2$.  Put $J=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}$,
$|T|\sim U[0,1]$,
\begin{equation*}
J=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.765196 .
\end{equation*}
For $i\ne j$

\begin{equation*}
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1dE|T_{i}-T_{j}|+\frac{d-1}{d}J
 =\frac{\,2/3+(d-1)J\,}{d}\equiv E_{d},
\qquad E|T_{i}-T_{j}|=2/3 .
\end{equation*}
The mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of the
$N_{d}=d+1$ points of $S_{d}$ is

\begin{equation*}
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE|X_{i}|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}J\,}{d(d+1)} ,
\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2 ,
\end{equation*}
and with $R_{d}=EV_{d}/\bar D_{d}$

\begin{equation*}
R_{d}
 =\frac{(2d)^{-d}(d+1)}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
 =\frac{3(d+1)}
        {2^{d}d^{\,d-1}\!\left[\,5d-2+(d-1)^{2}C\right]},\qquad 
C=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)=3J,
\end{equation*}
$R_{1}=1$.  In particular

* $R_{1}=1.0000$,
* $R_{2}=3/[8\,(8+C)]\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Hence, with the origin included
average pair distance,

\begin{equation*}
S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots
 \approx1.0000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.117\;,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.1172$, essentially $1.000+0.109+0.008$,
the tail beyond $d=4$ being $<5\times10^{-4}$.

This is the i.i.d. cross sampling, origin-included, normalisation.
Remark.  With the one-point-per-axis, bijective, normalisation
$EV_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ and $\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)J]/(d+1)$ one gets
$R_{d}^{\rm bi}=(d+1)2^{-d}/\{d![1+(d-1)J]\}$ and
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm bi}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the
$1.250$ value usually quoted for the distinct-axis model.  The
point–point normalisation $EV_{d}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ gives in the
distinct-axis model $(e^{1/2}-1)/J\approx0.848$. ∎

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the wording is being read as i.i.d. with replacement on the cross, but the statement is about a set that is built on *distinct* mutually orthogonal open segments and the number of points and the number of segments match in dimension. That is the usual 1-to-1 convention: in dimension d we have d different axes e1,…,ed and we put one point on each of them,

Xi = Yi ei , Yi ~ Unif[-1,1] i.i.d.,

with the origin added. Then the simplex is non-degenerate by construction and

Vol d [conv{0,X1,…,Xd}] = |det[X1 … Xd]|/d! = ∏i |Yi| / d! .

Hence with E|Y|=1/2

E Vol d = 2^{-d}/d! ,    E Vol 1 = 1/2 .

On two different axes

E ||Xi-Xj|| = E sqrt(Yi²+Yj²) = J ,
J:= ∫0¹∫0¹ sqrt(u²+v²) du dv
  = [√2 + ln(1+√2)]/3 ≈0.765196 .

E ||Xi|| = E|Yi|=1/2 . For the d+1 points 0,X1,…,Xd the unordered
pair mean is

\bar D d = [ d·½ + (d choose 2) J ] / (d+1 choose 2)
        = [1+(d-1)J]/(d+1) ,

so that with the origin included

R d = E Vol d / \bar D d
    = (d+1)2^{-d} / [ d! (1+(d-1)J) ] ,  R1=1 .

Numerically

R1 =1.0000
R2 = 3·2^{-2} /[2!(1+J)] ≈0.2126
R3 = 4·2^{-3} /[3!(1+2J)] ≈0.0329
R4 = 5·2^{-4} /[4!(1+3J)] ≈0.00395
R5 ≈0.00038 …

R d = O(2^{-d}/d!) so the tail after d=4 is <10^{-3}. Summing,

S = Σ d≥1 R d ≈ 1.0000+0.2126+0.0329+0.00395+0.00038+…
   ≈1.2497≈1.250 .

In particular the first four terms already give 1.249, the infinite tail being negligible. This is the 1+0.212+0.033+… value that is obtained when the d points are required to lie on d different orthogonal arms, i.e. the distinct-axis / one point per line interpretation that the phrase “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments… with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ is meant to enforce. Conditioning on the non-degenerate event is implicit in the geometry; the d!/d^d deflation that appears in the i.i.d. with-replacement model is an artefact of allowing collisions, which would put positive mass on a degenerate hull of zero volume and is not the intended sampling.

The 1.117 value is the i.i.d. with-replacement model E Vol d = (2d)^{-d} with the same \bar D d. That model allows two points to fall on the same axis and therefore needs the permutation factor d!/d^{d}. With distinct axes by construction that factor is 1 and the volume is 2^{-d}/d!, giving the 1.250 sum above.

The $d+1$ point set is $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ with

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}},\qquad

i.i.d.  Put $E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{i}-T_{j}|=2/3$ and

$$
I:=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.765196 .
$$

On $\{A_{1},\ldots ,A_{d}\}$ a permutation, ${\mathbf P}=d!/d^{d}$,

$$
\bigl|{\rm det}[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]\bigr|=\prod_{i=1}^{d}|T_{i}|
$$

hence with ${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}\,S_{d})=|{\rm det}|/d!$

$$

      =\frac{1}{(2d)^{d}},\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=
\frac1dE|T_{i}-T_{j}|+\frac{d-1}{d}I
   =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I}{d}=:E_{d},
$$

and with $E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ the mean unordered pair distance of the
$d+1$ points is

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE\|X\|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5d-2}{3}+I(d-1)^{2}}{d(d+1)} .
$$

Hence with $C=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)=3I$

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}
            {2^{d}d^{\,d-1}\Bigl[\dfrac{5d-2}{3}+I(d-1)^{2}\Bigr]}
     =\frac{3(d+1)}
            {2^{d}d^{\,d-1}\bigl[\,5d-2+(d-1)^{2}C\bigr]},\qquad
R_{1}=1 .
$$

In particular

* $R_{1}=1.0000$
* $R_{2}=3/\!\left[8\bigl(8+C\bigr)\right]\approx0.10928$
* $R_{3}\approx7.50\times10^{-3}$
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5},\ldots$

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$ so the series is exhausted after
$d=4$.  Numerically

$$

 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
 \approx1+0.10928+0.00750+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117
$$

to three decimals, $1.117$ with the $d=1$ term retained and

average-over-all-$\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs, normalisation.  With the

$R_{d}^{\sharp}=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)I)]$ and
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the familiar

$1.25$ value quoted for the $1\!:\!1$ line–point model. ∎

12.text:
For the cross
${\cal C}_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ let

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},
\qquad T_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}(-1,1) $$
i.i.d.  Put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ and
$|T|\sim {\rm Unif}(0,1)$.  Then $E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$I_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log (1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.7651957\ldots $$
On $\{K_{1},\ldots ,K_{d}{\rm\ a\ permutation}\}$,
${\bf P}\{K_{1},\ldots ,K_{d}{\rm\ a\ permutation}\}=d!/d^{\,d}$ and

$$
\det [X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]
   =\operatorname{sgn}\pi\prod_{i=1}^{d}T_{i},
$$

so that with $V_{d}(S_{d})={\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}S_{d}\bigr)$

$$
E V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{\,d}}\frac1{d!}\bigl(E|T|\bigr)^{d}
       =\frac{1}{(2d)^{d}},\qquad E V_{1}=1/2,
$$

and $E\|X_{i}\|=E|T|=1/2$.
For $i\ne j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
  =\frac1dE|T_{i}-T_{j}|+\frac{d-1}{d}I_{0}
  =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I_{0}}{d}=:E_{d},
$$

so that for the $d+1$ points the mean distance of a uniformly chosen
unordered pair is

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE\|X\|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}I_{0}\,}{d(d+1)} .
$$

Hence with $R_{d}=EV_{d}/\bar D_{d}\,$,

$$
R_{d}
 =\frac{(2d)^{-d}}{\bar D_{d}}
 =\frac{d+1}{2^{d}d^{\,d-1}\Bigl[\dfrac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}I_{0}\Bigr]}
 , \qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

and $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.0000$,
* $R_{2}=3\big/\!\bigl[8\bigl(8/3+I_{0}\bigr)\bigr]\approx0.10928$,
* $R_{3}=4\big/\!\bigl[72\bigl(13/3+4I_{0}\bigr)\bigr]\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5},\dots$

so that the $d+1$–point average–pair series is in fact exhausted
after $d=3$–$4$,
$$
S_{\infty}
 =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
 \approx1+0.10928+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.117\!-\!1.118,
$$
i.e. $S_{\infty}\simeq1.117$ to three decimals, $S_{\infty}\approx1.1172$
with the conventional $I_{0}=[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)]/3$.
In particular $R_{1}=1$ and the non–trivial tail is
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$,
$R_{2}\approx0.109$, $R_{3}\approx0.0075$, etc.

This is the i.i.d. cross, origin–included, average-pair normalisation.
Remark.  In the usual one–point-per-axis convention $X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{i}$,
$Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$, $EV_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I_{0}$ and

$$
\bar D_{d}^{\,0}=\frac{1+(d-1)I_{0}}{d+1},
\qquad
R_{d}^{0}=\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I_{0}}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
$$

so that $\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{0}=1+0.2124+0.0329+0.00395+\cdots\approx1.250$,
the familiar $1.25$ one-point-per-axis value, and
$EV_{d}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=2^{-d}/[d!\,I_{0}]$ sums to
$(e^{1/2}-1)/I_{0}\approx0.848$.  The $1.117$ sum above is the
fully i.i.d. axis choice with the mean over all $\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs
of $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$. ∎

10.text:
On the $d$-cross $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}{\rm span}\{e_{k}\}\cap B_{1}$ write
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ with $T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ and $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}
\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d.  Put $O=0$ and $S_{d}=\{O,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.
On the permutation event $ {\rm P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \ is\ a\ 
perm.}\}=d!/d^{d}$

$$
\bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]\bigr|
   =\prod_{i=1}^{d}|T_{i}|\;{\bf 1}_{\{K{\rm\ perm.}\}}
$$

so that with ${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$

$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac{1}{d!}{\mathbb E}\bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]\bigr|
   =\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{(1/2)^{d}}{d!}
   =(2d)^{-d},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 ,
$$
and  

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2 ,\qquad 
{\mathbb E}|T_{i}-T_{j}|=2/3 .
$$

Put  

$$
I={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx 0.7651957 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|T_{i}-T_{j}|+\frac{d-1}{d}I
   =\frac{\,2/3+(d-1)I\,}{d}\; .
$$

Hence for the $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{d}$

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d{\mathbb E}\|X\|+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
        {\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{\,d+(d-1)2/3+(d-1)^{2}I\,}{d(d+1)}
 =\frac{(5d-2)/3+I(d-1)^{2}}{d(d+1)} ,
$$

and

$$
R_{d}
   :=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
          {(5d-2)/3+I(d-1)^{2}},\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

In particular

* $R_{1}=1.0000$,
* $R_{2}= {\rm  6/16}\big/\!\bigl(8/3+I\bigr)
       \approx 0.10927$,
* $R_{3}=1/\!\bigl[\,78+72I\,\bigr]
       \approx 7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  The series is therefore
essentially exhausted after $d=3$–$4$.  Summing the origin–included
pair average,

$$
S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx 1.117\!-\!1.118,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}\simeq1.12$, $S_{\infty}\approx1.117$ in the usual
three–figure normalisation.  The $d=1$ term is the trivial $1$ and the
non–trivial tail is $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$, $R_{2}\approx0.109$
being the dominant contribution.  This is the $ (2d)^{-d}/\bar D_{d}$
i.i.d. cross form.  Up to the conventional $1\!:\!1$ line–point
normalisation $ {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ this gives the
familiar $R_{d}^{\rm dist}=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\bigl(1+(d-1)I\bigr)]$ and
$\sum_{d}R_{d}^{\rm dist}\approx1.250$, the $1.250$ value quoted for the
one–point–per–axis model. ∎

public_text.1:
The wording is the key.  The candidate set is the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin in the unit ball and the ensemble that is added to $\{0\}$ contains exactly $d$ points and exactly $d$ distinct segments, the numbers matching.  That is a bijection points $\leftrightarrow$ lines, not an i.i.d. draw with replacement from the union.  Up to relabelling we may write

$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{i},\qquad U_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;i=1\ldots d$,

one point on each orthogonal arm.  On this model the $d$-simplex
$\operatorname{conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ is non-degenerate a.s. and

${\rm Vol}_{d}= \dfrac{|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]|}{d!}
             =\dfrac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|U_{i}|}{d!}$.

With $E|U|=1/2$

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \dfrac{(1/2)^{d}}{d!}=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad 
E|U|=1/2$,

the $d!/d^{d}$ factor that appears for sampling with replacement does not belong to the stated set-up, because replacement would allow two points on the same arm and would make the hull degenerate with positive probability, contrary to the “distinct mutually orthogonal… with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ requirement.

For two different arms

$\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\sqrt{U_{i}^{2}+U_{j}^{2}}$ and

$J:=E\sqrt{U_{i}^{2}+U_{j}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765196.$

Hence for the $d+1$ points $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$

$E d_{0i}=1/2,\qquad E d_{ij}=J,\;i\neq j$,

and the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of the set is

$\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 J}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)J}{d+1}$.

The dimension-wise ratio is therefore

$R_{d}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)2^{-d}}{d!\,[1+(d-1)J]},\qquad R_{1}=1$,

$R_{2}= \dfrac{3\cdot2^{-2}}{2(1+J)}\approx0.2126$,
$R_{3}= \dfrac{4\cdot2^{-3}}{6[1+2J]}\approx0.0329$,
$R_{4}\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$, $R_{5}\approx3.8\times10^{-4}$, …

The series is $O(2^{-d}/d!)$ and is essentially exhausted after $d=4$:

$S_{N}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =1+0.2126+0.0329+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497$,

i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.250$ to three decimals.  This is the $1\!:\!1$
line-point normalisation that follows directly from the stated distinct
arms interpretation and is the $1.250$ value obtained by Colleagues 1,2,
4 and 11 for the origin-included mean pairwise distance.  The
$(2d)^{-d}$ volume that appears in the with-replacement i.i.d. model is an
extra $d!/d^{d}$ permutation assumption not required by the text.
public_text.2:
For a $d$ point cross let $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ and $U_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d.
and put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  Put $|U|\sim U[0,1]$, 
${\mathbb E}|U|=1/2$ and

$$
I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt 2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx0.7651957 .
$$

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}\}$ a permutation, ${\mathbb P}\{K\ {\rm perm}\}
=d!/d^{d}$,

$$
\bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]\bigr|
   =\prod_{i=1}^{d}|U_{i}|\qquad{\rm on\ \,the\ \,permutation},
$$

so that with ${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}S_{d})=|\det|/d!$,

$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{({\mathbb E}|U|)^{d}}{d!}
   =\frac{1}{(2d)^{d}},\qquad {\mathbb E}|X_{i}|=\frac12 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|U_{1}-U_{2}|+\frac{d-1}{d}I
   =\frac{2}{3d}+\frac{d-1}{d}I ,
\qquad{\mathbb E}|U_{1}-U_{2}|=\frac23 .
$$

Hence for the $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{d}$

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\,{\mathbb E}|X_{i}|
       +\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
      {\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{\,{\rm d}+\,d(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
      {d(d+1)}
 =\frac{(5d-2)/3+I(d-1)^{2}}{d(d+1)} ,
$$

$\bar D_{1}=1/2$, and

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
            {(5d-2)/3+I(d-1)^{2}},\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

In closed form with $C=3I=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)$

$$
R_{d}=\frac{3(d+1)}
          {2^{d}d^{\,d-1}\!\left[\,5d-2+(d-1)^{2}C\right]},\qquad
R_{1}=1,
$$

i.e.

* $R_{1}=1.000000$,
* $R_{2}=0.10927\ldots$,
* $R_{3}=7.51\times10^{-3}\ldots$,
* $R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}\ldots$,
* $R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}\ldots$,

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Hence

$$
S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.117\;,
$$

$1.117\!-\!1.118$ in the usual numerical quadrature, $S_{\infty}\approx
1.1172$ unrounded.  In particular $R_{1}=1$ and the non-trivial tail
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$.

Remark.  With the conventional one–point–per–axis normalisation
$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{i}$, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}^{0}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{0}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$, so that

$$
R_{d}^{0}=\frac{(d+1)2^{-d}}{d!\,[1+(d-1)I]},\qquad
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{0}\approx1.000+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+\cdots\approx
1.250,
$$

the $1.250$ value normally quoted for the distinct-axes model.  The
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ point–point normalisation is
$(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$.
public_text.4:
For the cross

$$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}\subset{\mathbf R}^{d}$$

let

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},
\qquad T_{i}\sim {\rm U}[-1,1],$$

i.i.d.  Put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ and 
$V_{d}={\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}S_{d})$.  On 
$\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;is\;a\;permutation}\}$,
${\bf P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;perm.}\}=d!/d^{d}$,

$$|\det [X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i=1}^{d}|T_{i}| 
{\bf 1}_{\{K\;{\rm perm.}\}},\qquad 
V_{d}= \frac{|\det [X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!},$$

so that with $E|T|=1/2$

\begin{equation*}
E V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{(E|T|)^{d}}{d!}
       =\frac{1}{(2d)^{d}},\qquad E|X_{i}|=\frac12 ,
\end{equation*}
$EV_{1}=1/2$.  Put $J=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}$,
$|T|\sim U[0,1]$,
\begin{equation*}
J=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.765196 .
\end{equation*}
For $i\ne j$

\begin{equation*}
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1dE|T_{i}-T_{j}|+\frac{d-1}{d}J
 =\frac{\,2/3+(d-1)J\,}{d}\equiv E_{d},
\qquad E|T_{i}-T_{j}|=2/3 .
\end{equation*}
The mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of the
$N_{d}=d+1$ points of $S_{d}$ is

\begin{equation*}
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE|X_{i}|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}J\,}{d(d+1)} ,
\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2 ,
\end{equation*}
and with $R_{d}=EV_{d}/\bar D_{d}$

\begin{equation*}
R_{d}
 =\frac{(2d)^{-d}(d+1)}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
 =\frac{3(d+1)}
        {2^{d}d^{\,d-1}\!\left[\,5d-2+(d-1)^{2}C\right]},\qquad 
C=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)=3J,
\end{equation*}
$R_{1}=1$.  In particular

* $R_{1}=1.0000$,
* $R_{2}=3/[8\,(8+C)]\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Hence, with the origin included
average pair distance,

\begin{equation*}
S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots
 \approx1.0000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.117\;,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.1172$, essentially $1.000+0.109+0.008$,
the tail beyond $d=4$ being $<5\times10^{-4}$.

This is the i.i.d. cross sampling, origin-included, normalisation.
Remark.  With the one-point-per-axis, bijective, normalisation
$EV_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ and $\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)J]/(d+1)$ one gets
$R_{d}^{\rm bi}=(d+1)2^{-d}/\{d![1+(d-1)J]\}$ and
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm bi}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the
$1.250$ value usually quoted for the distinct-axis model.  The
point–point normalisation $EV_{d}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ gives in the
distinct-axis model $(e^{1/2}-1)/J\approx0.848$. ∎
public_text.5:
I think the wording is being read as i.i.d. with replacement on the cross, but the statement is about a set that is built on *distinct* mutually orthogonal open segments and the number of points and the number of segments match in dimension. That is the usual 1-to-1 convention: in dimension d we have d different axes e1,…,ed and we put one point on each of them,

Xi = Yi ei , Yi ~ Unif[-1,1] i.i.d.,

with the origin added. Then the simplex is non-degenerate by construction and

Vol d [conv{0,X1,…,Xd}] = |det[X1 … Xd]|/d! = ∏i |Yi| / d! .

Hence with E|Y|=1/2

E Vol d = 2^{-d}/d! ,    E Vol 1 = 1/2 .

On two different axes

E ||Xi-Xj|| = E sqrt(Yi²+Yj²) = J ,
J:= ∫0¹∫0¹ sqrt(u²+v²) du dv
  = [√2 + ln(1+√2)]/3 ≈0.765196 .

E ||Xi|| = E|Yi|=1/2 . For the d+1 points 0,X1,…,Xd the unordered
pair mean is

\bar D d = [ d·½ + (d choose 2) J ] / (d+1 choose 2)
        = [1+(d-1)J]/(d+1) ,

so that with the origin included

R d = E Vol d / \bar D d
    = (d+1)2^{-d} / [ d! (1+(d-1)J) ] ,  R1=1 .

Numerically

R1 =1.0000
R2 = 3·2^{-2} /[2!(1+J)] ≈0.2126
R3 = 4·2^{-3} /[3!(1+2J)] ≈0.0329
R4 = 5·2^{-4} /[4!(1+3J)] ≈0.00395
R5 ≈0.00038 …

R d = O(2^{-d}/d!) so the tail after d=4 is <10^{-3}. Summing,

S = Σ d≥1 R d ≈ 1.0000+0.2126+0.0329+0.00395+0.00038+…
   ≈1.2497≈1.250 .

In particular the first four terms already give 1.249, the infinite tail being negligible. This is the 1+0.212+0.033+… value that is obtained when the d points are required to lie on d different orthogonal arms, i.e. the distinct-axis / one point per line interpretation that the phrase “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments… with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ is meant to enforce. Conditioning on the non-degenerate event is implicit in the geometry; the d!/d^d deflation that appears in the i.i.d. with-replacement model is an artefact of allowing collisions, which would put positive mass on a degenerate hull of zero volume and is not the intended sampling.

The 1.117 value is the i.i.d. with-replacement model E Vol d = (2d)^{-d} with the same \bar D d. That model allows two points to fall on the same axis and therefore needs the permutation factor d!/d^{d}. With distinct axes by construction that factor is 1 and the volume is 2^{-d}/d!, giving the 1.250 sum above.

\qquad

$$

$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{( {\mathbb E}|U|)^{d}}{d^{\,d}}
      =(2d)^{-d}\;, \qquad {\mathbb E}|X|=1/2 .
$$

$|U|\sim{\rm U}(0,1)$ gives

$$
I=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}{3}
   =0.7651957\ldots

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|U_{i}-U_{j}|+\frac{d-1}{d}I
 =\frac{\,2/3+(d-1)I\,}{d}\;,\qquad {\mathbb E}|U_{i}-U_{j}|=2/3 .
$$

$$

 =\frac{d{\mathbb E}|X|+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
        {\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{d+1}\;,

I think the integral work in the i.i.d. camp is correct and the numerical value 
$I=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\bigl[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3\approx0.765196$
is the right mean inter-point distance on a pair of different arms. The point where the models diverge is the sampling of the axes.

The statement is a uniform process on the union of d distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin in the unit ball, with the number of points and the number of line segments matching the dimension. That is read in the usual geometric way as a one-to-one assignment: we have d labelled orthogonal arms and we put exactly one independent $U(-1,1)$ point on each arm. Two points are never allowed to fall on the same arm by construction; the ensemble is the d-tuple 
$X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{i},\;Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., up to relabelling of the axes.

On that model the simplex $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ is always non-degenerate and

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}\{0,X_{i}\})=|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|/d!
   =\prod_{i=1}^{d}|Y_{i}|/d!$,

so with $E|Y|=1/2$

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$,

no $d!/d^{d}$ factor. The $d!/d^{d}$ that appears in 10,12,3,6,8 is the probability that $d$ i.i.d. axis choices happen to be a permutation. Conditioning on a permutation is exactly imposing the distinct-arm requirement that the wording already imposes, so the unconditional i.i.d. with replacement expectation is not the expectation of the described ensemble.

For the $d+1$ points $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ we have $E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ and for $i\ne j$ $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I$. Hence the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of the set that the problem asks for is

$\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\,E\|X\|+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
        =\frac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1}$,

which is the origin-included average used by 1,2,4. The dimension-wise ratio is therefore

$R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}
     =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad R_{1}=1,$

i.e. $R_{d}= (d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl[d!\,\bigl(1+(d-1)I\bigr)\bigr]$.

Numerically
$R_{1}=1.0000$,
$R_{2}=3\cdot2^{-2}/\bigl[2(1+I)\bigr]\approx0.2126$,
$R_{3}=4\cdot2^{-3}/\bigl[6(1+2I)\bigr]\approx0.0329$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$, $R_{5}\approx0.00038$,
and the tail is $O(2^{-d}/d!)$.

Summing,

$S=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\approx1.0000+0.2126+0.0329+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497$,

i.e. $1.250$ to three decimals, essentially exhausted after $d=4$. This is the $1:1$ line-point normalisation that 1,2,4 quote. 

The $1.117$ value is the same calculation but with i.i.d. axis choice with replacement, i.e. with the $d!/d^{d}$ collision penalty kept in the volume expectation $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$. Once the distinct-arm requirement is enforced that penalty is removed and the familiar $2^{-d}/d!$ volume returns, which is why the series sits at $\approx1.25$ rather than $\approx1.12$. The integral $I$ and the $d+1$ origin-included averaging are the same in both camps; the only modelling choice is with or without replacement across the $d$ orthogonal segments, and the wording points to without replacement.

The wording is a one-to-one assignment of points to lines.  
The support is the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments
$L_{k}= \{t e_{k} :0<|t|<1\}$ in the unit ball and we add $d$ independent
stochastic points, one on each line.  Up to relabelling

$$X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{i},\qquad Y_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1)\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad i=1,\dots ,d ,$$

and $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  On this event the simplex is
non-degenerate a.s. and

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}S_{d}\bigr)=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
      =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|Y_{i}|}{d!},$$

so that with $E|Y|=1/2$

$$E\,{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{(E|Y|)^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad 
E\,{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 .$$

Let $I=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}$ for $U,V\sim {\rm Unif}(0,1)$ i.i.d.  Then

$$I=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.765196 .$$

For $i\ne j$

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\| =E\sqrt{Y_{i}^{2}+Y_{j}^{2}}=I,\qquad 
E\|X_{i}\|=E|Y_{i}|=1/2 .$$

The mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of the $d+1$
points $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ is therefore

$$\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\,E\|X_{i}\|+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{d/2+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1},$$

and $\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  Hence with the usual origin-included average

$$R_{d}:=\frac{E\,{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
      =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I}\,\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad R_{1}=1.$$

In closed form

$$R_{d}= \frac{(d+1)2^{-d}}{d!\,[1+(d-1)I]},\qquad 
I=\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}.$$

Numerically

$\,R_{1}=1.0000$,\,
$R_{2}=2\cdot2^{-2}/[1\cdot(1+I)]\approx0.2126$,\,
$R_{3}=3\cdot2^{-3}/[2\,(1+2I)]\approx0.0329$,\,
$R_{4}\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$,\,
$R_{5}\approx3.8\times10^{-4}$,

and $R_{d}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$ so the tail beyond $d=5$ is $<10^{-4}$.
Summation

$$S=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
  =1+0.2126+0.0329+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.2497,$$

i.e. $S\approx1.250$ to three decimals, essentially $1+0.212+0.033+\cdots$.
This is the $1\!:\!1$ line–point normalisation usually quoted for the
cross, $E\,{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ and the origin-included mean pairwise
distance $\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$.

The $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor $E\,{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ obtained by
allowing the $d$ points to be i.i.d. on the whole cross with replacement
is a different sampling model: it gives a positive probability of two
points sharing a line, hence ${\rm Vol}_{d}=0$ with probability
$1-d!/d^{d}$, and is not the distinct-lines interpretation implied by
“$d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments … with the number
of such points and line segments matching the dimension”.  With the
intended distinct-lines assignment the volume is $2^{-d}/d!$ and the
origin-included average pairwise distance is $[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$, giving the
familiar $1.25$ sum.

The description is a bijection, not an i.i.d. draw from the union.

The set is the origin together with one independent uniform point on each of the d distinct mutually orthogonal open segments in the unit ball. Writing the i-th point as X_i = Y_i e_i with Y_i ∼ Unif[-1,1] i.i.d. and {e_i} an orthonormal basis, the convex hull is the ordinary simplex

conv{0,X_1,…,X_d} with 
Vol_d = |det[X_1 … X_d]|/d! = |Y_1⋯Y_d|/d! .

Hence unconditionally on the construction

E Vol_d = (E|Y|)^d / d! = 2^{-d}/d!,   E|Y| = 1/2,
E Vol_1 = 1/2,

which is the usual 1/d! simplex volume.  The factor d!/d^d that appears in the i.i.d. axis model is an artefact of allowing collisions L_i = L_j.  With one point per distinct orthogonal segment collisions are excluded by construction, and conditioning on general position is built in.  The permutation probability d!/d^d is therefore not part of the model.

For the pairwise distances put a = E|Y| = 1/2 and

J = E sqrt(Y_1^2+Y_2^2)=∫_0^1∫_0^1 sqrt(u^2+v^2)du dv
  = [√2+log(1+√2)]/3 ≈ 0.765196 .

On distinct arms E‖X_i‖ = a and for i≠j E‖X_i-X_j‖ = J.  For the d+1 points {0,X_1,…,X_d} the mean unordered pairwise distance is

\bar D_d = [ d a + \binom d2 J ] / \binom{d+1}{2}
        = [2a+(d-1)J]/(d+1)
        = [1+(d-1)J]/(d+1),

with \bar D_1 = a = 1/2.

The dimension-wise ratio is therefore

R_d = E Vol_d / \bar D_d
    = (d+1)2^{-d} / [ d! (1+(d-1)J) ],   R_1 =1,

i.e. the familiar one-point-per-arm normalisation.  Numerically

R_1 =1.0000,
R_2 = 3·2^{-2} / [2! (1+J)] ≈0.2126,
R_3 = 4·2^{-3} / [3! (1+2J)] ≈0.0329,
R_4 = 5·2^{-4} / [4! (1+3J)] ≈0.00395,
R_5 ≈0.00038, …

R_d = O(2^{-d}/d!) so the series is exhausted after d=4.  Summing,

S = Σ_{d≥1} R_d ≈1.0000+0.2126+0.0329+0.00395+0.00038+…
  ≈1.2497≈1.250

to three decimals.  This is the 1 + 0.212 + 0.033 + … value obtained with the natural distinct-axes reading of the cross and with the mean pairwise distance taken over the whole set {0,X_1,…,X_d}.  The i.i.d. axis model that multiplies the volume by d!/d^d and uses an unconditional expectation forces a vanishing volume with probability 1−d!/d^d, which is inconsistent with the statement that the number of points and the number of distinct orthogonal segments match.  Once the bijection is imposed the 1.25 sum is the consistent one.

$$

so that with $V_{d}(S_{d})={\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}S_{d}\bigr)$

$$
E V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{\,d}}\frac1{d!}\bigl(E|T|\bigr)^{d}
       =\frac{1}{(2d)^{d}},\qquad E V_{1}=1/2,
$$

and $E\|X_{i}\|=E|T|=1/2$.
For $i\ne j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
  =\frac1dE|T_{i}-T_{j}|+\frac{d-1}{d}I_{0}
  =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I_{0}}{d}=:E_{d},
$$

so that for the $d+1$ points the mean distance of a uniformly chosen
unordered pair is

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE\|X\|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{\,\dfrac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}I_{0}\,}{d(d+1)} .
$$

Hence with $R_{d}=EV_{d}/\bar D_{d}\,$,

$$
R_{d}
 =\frac{(2d)^{-d}}{\bar D_{d}}
 =\frac{d+1}{2^{d}d^{\,d-1}\Bigl[\dfrac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}I_{0}\Bigr]}
 , \qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

and $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.0000$,
* $R_{2}=3\big/\!\bigl[8\bigl(8/3+I_{0}\bigr)\bigr]\approx0.10928$,
* $R_{3}=4\big/\!\bigl[72\bigl(13/3+4I_{0}\bigr)\bigr]\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5},\dots$

so that the $d+1$–point average–pair series is in fact exhausted
after $d=3$–$4$,
$$
S_{\infty}
 =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
 \approx1+0.10928+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.117\!-\!1.118,
$$
i.e. $S_{\infty}\simeq1.117$ to three decimals, $S_{\infty}\approx1.1172$
with the conventional $I_{0}=[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)]/3$.
In particular $R_{1}=1$ and the non–trivial tail is
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$,
$R_{2}\approx0.109$, $R_{3}\approx0.0075$, etc.

This is the i.i.d. cross, origin–included, average-pair normalisation.
Remark.  In the usual one–point-per-axis convention $X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{i}$,
$Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$, $EV_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I_{0}$ and

$$
\bar D_{d}^{\,0}=\frac{1+(d-1)I_{0}}{d+1},
\qquad
R_{d}^{0}=\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I_{0}}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
$$

so that $\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{0}=1+0.2124+0.0329+0.00395+\cdots\approx1.250$,
the familiar $1.25$ one-point-per-axis value, and
$EV_{d}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=2^{-d}/[d!\,I_{0}]$ sums to
$(e^{1/2}-1)/I_{0}\approx0.848$.  The $1.117$ sum above is the
fully i.i.d. axis choice with the mean over all $\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs
of $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$. ∎
public_text.10:
On the $d$-cross $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}{\rm span}\{e_{k}\}\cap B_{1}$ write

On the permutation event $ {\rm P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \ is\ a\ 
perm.}\}=d!/d^{d}$

$$
\bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]\bigr|
   =\prod_{i=1}^{d}|T_{i}|\;{\bf 1}_{\{K{\rm\ perm.}\}}
$$

so that with ${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$

$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac{1}{d!}{\mathbb E}\bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]\bigr|
   =\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{(1/2)^{d}}{d!}
   =(2d)^{-d},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 ,
$$
and  

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2 ,\qquad 
{\mathbb E}|T_{i}-T_{j}|=2/3 .
$$

$$
I={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx 0.7651957 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|T_{i}-T_{j}|+\frac{d-1}{d}I
   =\frac{\,2/3+(d-1)I\,}{d}\; .
$$

Hence for the $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{d}$

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d{\mathbb E}\|X\|+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
        {\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{\,d+(d-1)2/3+(d-1)^{2}I\,}{d(d+1)}
 =\frac{(5d-2)/3+I(d-1)^{2}}{d(d+1)} ,
$$

and

$$
R_{d}
   :=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
          {(5d-2)/3+I(d-1)^{2}},\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots

$$

*i.i.d. cross / with-replacement reading.* $X_i=U_i e_{K_i}$, $U_i\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d. On a permutation
$|\det[X_1..X_d]|=\prod|U_i|$ and ${\mathbb P}\{K\text{ perm}\}=d!/d^d$.

$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]/(d+1)

The disagreement is purely the axis assignment: bijection points $\leftrightarrow$ arms vs i.i.d. draw from the union with replacement. The distinct-arms wording favours the $2^{-d}/d!$ volume and the $1.250$ sum. 12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The round-1 discussion re-states the two modelling choices that were already present in round 0 and sharpens the wording argument.

One-point-per-arm / bijection model.  Up to relabelling $X_i=Y_i e_i$, $Y_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., one point on each of the $d$ distinct orthogonal arms.  Then
${\rm Vol}_d=|\det[X_1\ldots X_d]|/d!=\prod|Y_i|/d!$, $E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$, $E|X_i|=1/2$ and for $i\neq j$
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{Y_1^2+Y_2^2}=J$ with 
$J=\int_0^1\!\int_0^1\sqrt{u^2+v^2}du dv=[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)]/3\approx0.765196$.
For the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_i\}$ the mean unordered pair distance is
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)J]/(d+1)$ and
$R_d=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)J)]$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.2126$, $R_3\approx0.0329$, $R_4\approx0.00395$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.  This is the $1.25$ value repeated by Colleagues 1,2,4,7,11,13,14,5.

Fully i.i.d. axis choice with replacement.  $X_i=T_i e_{K_i}$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$ i.i.d., $T_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.  Permutation probability $d!/d^{d}$ gives
$E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$, $E|X|=1/2$, $E|T_i-T_j|=2/3$ and
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=[2/3+(d-1)J]/d=:E_d$.
The origin-included mean pair distance is
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)E_d]/(d+1)=[(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^2J]/[d(d+1)]$ and
$R_d^{\rm iid}=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)/[2^{d}d^{\,d-1}((5d-2)/3+(d-1)^2J)]$.
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.1093$, $R_3\approx0.0075$, $R_4\approx3.8\times10^{-4}$,

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is still split on two modelling choices and on the precise denominator.

*Distinct one-point-per-arm / bijective model* – the reading that “d distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments … with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ forces a bijection points↔arms. Up to relabelling $X_i=Y_i e_i$, $Y_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.
$E{\rm Vol}_d = (E|Y|)^d/d! =2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_i\|=1/2$.
$E\|X_i-X_j\| = J$ for $i\ne j$ with
$J=E\sqrt{Y_1^2+Y_2^2}=\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1\sqrt{u^2+v^2}dudv
 =[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)]/3\approx0.765196$.
For the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_i\}$ the mean unordered pair distance is
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)J]/(d+1)$.
Hence
$R_d^{\rm dist}=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl[d!\,(1+(d-1)J)\bigr]$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.2126$, $R_3\approx0.0329$, $R_4\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$,
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm dist}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
Point-point normalisation $E{\rm Vol}_d/E\|X_i-X_j\|=2^{-d}/(d!J)$ sums to
$(e^{1/2}-1)/J\approx0.8478$.

*i.i.d. axis choice with replacement* – the literal “independent stochastic points on the union of the $d$ axes’’.
$X_i=T_i e_{K_i}$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$, $T_i\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d.
${\mathbb P}\{K_1..K_d$ a permutation$\}=d!/d^d$ and
$E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$, $E\|X_i\|=1/2$.
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=[2/3+(d-1)J]/d$, $E|T_i-T_j|=2/3$.
Mean unordered pair distance on $\{0,X_i\}$:
$\bar D_d^{\rm iid}=[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]/(d+1)
 =\big[(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^2J\big]/[d(d+1)]$.
$R_d^{\rm iid}=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d^{\rm iid}
 =3(d+1)/\bigl[2^d d^{\,d-1}\bigl(5d-2+(d-1)^2C\bigr)\bigr]$,
$C=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)=3J$.
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm iid}\approx1.1172\approx1.117$,
tail $\approx0.117$ beyond $d=1$. With the usual $X\!-\!X$ denominator
$E\|X_i-X_j\|$ the non-trivial sum is $\approx0.094$.

Round 1 public positions:
- Colleagues 1,13,14,5,9 argue the distinct-arms reading is forced by the
text and give $S\approx1.250$ for the origin-included mean pair distance,
with the $2^{-d}/d!$ volume.
- Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 present the i.i.d. with-replacement model,
give $E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$ and $S\approx1.117$ for the origin-included
mean pair, and note the $1.250$ distinct-arms value as the $1\!:\!1$ limit.
- Repeated numerical constants: $J\approx0.765196$, $C\approx2.295588$,
$E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_i-T_j|=2/3$.
- Remaining ambiguities: whether the denominator is the mean over all
$\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs including the origin, $\bar D_d$, or the generic
point-point mean $E\|X_i-X_j\|$, and whether the $d!/d^d$ permutation
penalty belongs in the model. The “independent stochastic points’’ wording
favours i.i.d., the “distinct segments … number matching dimension’’
wording favours the bijective one-point-per-arm model. The rapid
$(2d)^{-d}$ decay makes the i.i.d. series essentially $1+0.109+0.008+O(10^{-4})$,
whereas the distinct series is $1+0.212+0.033+0.004+O(10^{-4})$.

No consensus yet; the two most cited three-decimal values are $1.250$
for the distinct-arms origin-included average and $1.117$ for the i.i.d.
origin-included average, with the point-point distinct normalisation
$(e^{1/2}-1)/J\approx0.848$ also frequently quoted.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is split between a 1-to-1 line-point / permutation model and the i.i.d. with-replacement sampling from the cross. 

* Distinct-arm / permutation model: $X_i=Y_i e_i$, $Y_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., one point per arm by construction. 
$E Vol_d =2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_i\|=1/2$, $E\|X_i-X_j\|=S$ with
$S=E\sqrt{U^2+V^2}= \int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1\sqrt{u^2+v^2}du dv
=(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.7651957$.
Mean unordered pair distance of $\{0,X_i\}$ is 
$\bar D_d^{\rm perm}=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1)$ and
$R_d^{\rm perm}=(d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl[d!\,(1+(d-1)S)\bigr]$, $R_1=1$.
Numerically $R_2\approx0.2126$, $R_3\approx0.0329$, $R_4\approx0.00395$, 
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm perm}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$. 
This is the 1.25 value quoted by Colleagues 1,2,4,11,13,14,5,7.

* i.i.d. cross model: $X_i=U_i e_{K_i}$, $U_i\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d.
Permutation event has probability $d!/d^{d}$. 
$E Vol_d=(2d)^{-d}$, $E|X|=1/2$, $E|U_i-U_j|=2/3$, 
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=E_d=[2/3+(d-1)S]/d$.
Mean unordered pair distance of $\{0,X_i\}$ is 
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)E_d]/(d+1)=\bigl[(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^2S\bigr]/[d(d+1)]$.
$R_d=(2d)^{-d}(d+1)/[1+(d-1)E_d]$.
Numerically $R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_5\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$, tail $O((2d)^{-d})$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1+0.10927+0.00752+0.00038\approx1.117\!-\!1.118$, 
$\approx1.1172$ with $S=(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3$.
The non-trivial tail $\sum_{d\ge2}R_d\approx0.117$, $R_2$ dominates.

The wording “ensemble of independent stochastic points’’ and “uniform stochastic process on the union’’ points to i.i.d. sampling from the union with replacement, i.e. the $(2d)^{-d}$ volume. The “number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’ is then just a description of the support, not a forced injection. Colleagues 1,5,7,13,14 argue the bijection / distinct-arm reading is intended and give the $1.250$ sum; Colleagues 10,11,12,3,6,8 give the i.i.d. $1.117$ sum. The integral $S$ is stable to $10^{-4}$; the series is super-exponentially convergent and essentially $1+R_2+R_3$. Unresolved is whether the problem intends the conditional-on-permutation / one-point-per-arm normalisation, which removes the $d!/d^{d}$ factor and gives the familiar $2^{-d}/d!$ volume and $1.250$ sum, or the unconditional i.i.d. model which is the literal independent-sampling interpretation and gives $\approx1.117$, $\approx1.12$ to two figures. Unresolved is which sampling interpretation the problem intends. Both the integral $J$ and the origin-included mean $\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)J]/(d+1)$ are agreed upon; the divergence is the $d!/d^{d}$ permutation factor in the volume expectation and hence $2^{-d}/d!$ vs $(2d)^{-d}$. reflection_text.3:
The discussion remains split between two sampling interpretations of the cross $\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_k\subset B_1$.

*One-to-one / distinct-arm reading.* $X_i=Y_i e_i$, $Y_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., one point per fixed orthogonal arm, $S_d=\{0,X_1..X_d\}$. Then
${\rm Vol}_d = \prod_i|Y_i|/d!$, $E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$, $E|X_i|=1/2$,
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=J$ with $J=E\sqrt{U^2+V^2}=\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1\sqrt{u^2+v^2}du dv
=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.765196$.
Origin-included mean unordered pair distance
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)J]/(d+1)$.
$R_d^{(1)}=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)J)]$, $R_1=1$,
$R_2\approx0.2126$, $R_3\approx0.0329$, $R_4\approx3.95e-3$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{(1)}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
Point-point normalisation $E{\rm Vol}_d/J$ sums to $(e^{1/2}-1)/J\approx0.848$.
This is the $1.25$ value pushed by Colleagues 1,13,14,5,7,9 and the
$1\!:\!1$ remark in 2,10,11,12.

*i.i.d. cross / with-replacement reading.* $X_i=U_i e_{K_i}$, $U_i\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d. On a permutation
$|\det[X_1..X_d]|=\prod|U_i|$ and ${\mathbb P}\{K\text{ perm}\}=d!/d^d$.
Hence $E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$, $E|X|=1/2$,
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=[2/3+(d-1)J]/d$, and with the origin included
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]/(d+1)
=[(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^2J]/[d(d+1)]$.
Then $R_d^{(iid)}=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]$
$=3(d+1)/[2^{d}d^{d-1}(5d-2+(d-1)^2C)]$ with $C=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)$.
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx7.51e-3$, $R_4\approx3.79e-4$,
$R_5\approx1.5e-5$. $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{(iid)}\approx1.000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038\approx1.117\!-\!1.118$, $\approx1.117$ to three decimals.
The $d\ge2$ tail is $\approx0.117$. This is the $1.117\approx1.12$ consensus of Colleagues 10,11,12,3,4,6,8.

The disagreement is purely the axis assignment: bijection points $\leftrightarrow$ arms vs i.i.d. draw from the union with replacement. The literal “uniform stochastic process on the union’’ wording favours the i.i.d. $ (2d)^{-d}$ volume and the $1.117$ sum with origin-included $\bar D_d$. The distinct-arms wording favours the $2^{-d}/d!$ volume and the $1.250$ sum. Integral $J$ and the origin-included averaging $\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)J]/(d+1)$ are now agreed on both sides; the remaining unresolved issue is whether the $d!/d^d$ permutation penalty belongs in the expectation.
reflection_text.12:
The round-1 discussion re-states the two modelling choices that were already present in round 0 and sharpens the wording argument.

One-point-per-arm / bijection model.  Up to relabelling $X_i=Y_i e_i$, $Y_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., one point on each of the $d$ distinct orthogonal arms.  Then
${\rm Vol}_d=|\det[X_1\ldots X_d]|/d!=\prod|Y_i|/d!$, $E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$, $E|X_i|=1/2$ and for $i\neq j$
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{Y_1^2+Y_2^2}=J$ with 
$J=\int_0^1\!\int_0^1\sqrt{u^2+v^2}du dv=[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)]/3\approx0.765196$.
For the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_i\}$ the mean unordered pair distance is
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)J]/(d+1)$ and
$R_d=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)J)]$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.2126$, $R_3\approx0.0329$, $R_4\approx0.00395$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.  This is the $1.25$ value repeated by Colleagues 1,2,4,7,11,13,14,5.

Fully i.i.d. axis choice with replacement.  $X_i=T_i e_{K_i}$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$ i.i.d., $T_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.  Permutation probability $d!/d^{d}$ gives
$E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$, $E|X|=1/2$, $E|T_i-T_j|=2/3$ and
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=[2/3+(d-1)J]/d=:E_d$.
The origin-included mean pair distance is
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)E_d]/(d+1)=[(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^2J]/[d(d+1)]$ and
$R_d^{\rm iid}=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)/[2^{d}d^{\,d-1}((5d-2)/3+(d-1)^2J)]$.
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.1093$, $R_3\approx0.0075$, $R_4\approx3.8\times10^{-4}$,
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm iid}\approx1.117\!-\!1.118$.  This is the $1.117$ value repeated by Colleagues 10,11,12,3,6,8.

Normalization variants: point-point $E{\rm Vol}_d/E\|X_i-X_j\|$ gives $(e^{1/2}-1)/J\approx0.848$ in the bijection model and $R_d^{pp}=(2d)^{-d}/E_d$ summing to $\approx0.094$ non-trivial tail in the i.i.d. model.

Unresolved: the phrase “union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments… with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ is read by 1,13,14,7 as imposing a bijection, i.e. one point per distinct arm, no $d!/d^{d}$ deflation and $E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$.  The i.i.d. camp reads “independent stochastic points on the union’’ as independent draws with replacement from the whole cross, giving the $d!/d^{d}$ volume deflation and the $\approx1.117$ sum.  The integral $J$ and the origin-included averaging $[1+(d-1)J]/(d+1)$ are common to both camps; the disagreement is purely the $d!/d^{d}$ permutation factor and whether the pairwise mean is taken over the $d+1$ set or point-point.  Numerical coarse integration errors, e.g. the Simpson $m\approx0.768$ yielding $1.122$, are noted as artefacts. ∎
reflection_text.4:
The discussion is still split on two modelling choices and on the precise denominator.

*Distinct one-point-per-arm / bijective model* – the reading that “d distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments … with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ forces a bijection points↔arms. Up to relabelling $X_i=Y_i e_i$, $Y_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.
$E{\rm Vol}_d = (E|Y|)^d/d! =2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_i\|=1/2$.
$E\|X_i-X_j\| = J$ for $i\ne j$ with
$J=E\sqrt{Y_1^2+Y_2^2}=\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1\sqrt{u^2+v^2}dudv
 =[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)]/3\approx0.765196$.
For the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_i\}$ the mean unordered pair distance is
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)J]/(d+1)$.
Hence
$R_d^{\rm dist}=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl[d!\,(1+(d-1)J)\bigr]$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.2126$, $R_3\approx0.0329$, $R_4\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$,
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm dist}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
Point-point normalisation $E{\rm Vol}_d/E\|X_i-X_j\|=2^{-d}/(d!J)$ sums to
$(e^{1/2}-1)/J\approx0.8478$.

*i.i.d. axis choice with replacement* – the literal “independent stochastic points on the union of the $d$ axes’’.
$X_i=T_i e_{K_i}$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$, $T_i\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d.
${\mathbb P}\{K_1..K_d$ a permutation$\}=d!/d^d$ and
$E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$, $E\|X_i\|=1/2$.
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=[2/3+(d-1)J]/d$, $E|T_i-T_j|=2/3$.
Mean unordered pair distance on $\{0,X_i\}$:
$\bar D_d^{\rm iid}=[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]/(d+1)
 =\big[(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^2J\big]/[d(d+1)]$.
$R_d^{\rm iid}=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d^{\rm iid}
 =3(d+1)/\bigl[2^d d^{\,d-1}\bigl(5d-2+(d-1)^2C\bigr)\bigr]$,
$C=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)=3J$.
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm iid}\approx1.1172\approx1.117$,
tail $\approx0.117$ beyond $d=1$. With the usual $X\!-\!X$ denominator
$E\|X_i-X_j\|$ the non-trivial sum is $\approx0.094$.

Round 1 public positions:
- Colleagues 1,13,14,5,9 argue the distinct-arms reading is forced by the
text and give $S\approx1.250$ for the origin-included mean pair distance,
with the $2^{-d}/d!$ volume.
- Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 present the i.i.d. with-replacement model,
give $E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$ and $S\approx1.117$ for the origin-included
mean pair, and note the $1.250$ distinct-arms value as the $1\!:\!1$ limit.
- Repeated numerical constants: $J\approx0.765196$, $C\approx2.295588$,
$E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_i-T_j|=2/3$.
- Remaining ambiguities: whether the denominator is the mean over all
$\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs including the origin, $\bar D_d$, or the generic
point-point mean $E\|X_i-X_j\|$, and whether the $d!/d^d$ permutation
penalty belongs in the model. The “independent stochastic points’’ wording
favours i.i.d., the “distinct segments … number matching dimension’’
wording favours the bijective one-point-per-arm model. The rapid
$(2d)^{-d}$ decay makes the i.i.d. series essentially $1+0.109+0.008+O(10^{-4})$,
whereas the distinct series is $1+0.212+0.033+0.004+O(10^{-4})$.

No consensus yet; the two most cited three-decimal values are $1.250$
for the distinct-arms origin-included average and $1.117$ for the i.i.d.
origin-included average, with the point-point distinct normalisation
$(e^{1/2}-1)/J\approx0.848$ also frequently quoted.

reflection_text.6:
The deliberation is split on sampling and on the normalisation of the pairwise distance.

Sampling.
* Distinct-arm / one point per arm. Up to relabelling $X_i=Y_i e_i$, $Y_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d. 
$E|Y|=1/2$, $E{\rm Vol}_d = (E|Y|)^d/d! =2^{-d}/d!$, a.s. non-degenerate.  
$J:=E\sqrt{Y_1^2+Y_2^2}= \int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1\sqrt{u^2+v^2}du dv
 =\bigl[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3\approx0.765196$.  
For the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_i\}$ $E\|X_i\|=1/2$, $E\|X_i-X_j\|=J$, $i\ne j$, 
$\bar D_d=\bigl[d/2+\binom d2J\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}=[1+(d-1)J]/(d+1)$,
$R_d^{\sharp}=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl[d!\bigl(1+(d-1)J\bigr)\bigr]$,
$R_1=1,\;R_2\approx0.2126,\;R_3\approx0.0329,\;R_4\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\sharp}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.  
Point-point normalisation $E{\rm Vol}_d/J=2^{-d}/(d!J)$ sums to $(e^{1/2}-1)/J\approx0.8478$.

* i.i.d. from the whole cross with replacement. $X_i=T_i e_{A_i}$, $A_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d., $T_i\sim U(-1,1)$. 
${\mathbb P}\{A_1\ldots A_d{\rm\;perm.}\}=d!/d^{d}$, on the permutation event $|\det[X_1\ldots X_d]|=\prod|T_i|$. 
$E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$, $E|X|=1/2$, $E|T_i-T_j|=2/3$.
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=d^{-1}2/3+(d-1)d^{-1}I$ with $I=J\approx0.765196$.
For $\{0,X_i\}$ $\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]/(d+1)
 =\bigl[(5d-2)/3+I(d-1)^2\bigr]/[d(d+1)]$.
$R_d^{\rm iid}=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d
 =3(d+1)/\bigl\{2^{d}d^{\,d-1}\bigl[5d-2+(d-1)^2C\bigr]\bigr\}$,
$C=3I=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)$, $R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.1093$, $R_3\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm iid}\approx1.1172\approx1.117$.
Point-point version $R_d^{pp}= (2d)^{-d}d/[2/3+(d-1)I]$ sums to $\approx1.094$, $d\ge2$ tail $\approx0.094$.

The wording “union of d distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments … with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ is argued by Colleagues 1,13,14,7,5,9 to enforce the bijection one point per distinct arm, i.e. the $2^{-d}/d!$ volume and the $1.250$ origin-included sum.  The literal i.i.d. from the union reading keeps the $d!/d^{d}$ permutation penalty, giving $(2d)^{-d}$ volume and the $\approx1.117$ origin-included sum, as in Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8.

Unresolved: whether the stated “distinct’’ segments and “matching numbers’’ is a sampling constraint forbidding collisions, hence the distinct-arm $1.250$ value, or merely a description of the support, hence the i.i.d. with-replacement $1.117$ value.  The pairwise normalisation is the origin-included average over $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs in the current working reading; the point-point normalisation is a well known variant.  The $1.250$ distinct-arm origin-included series is the literature $1+0.212+0.033+\dots$ value, the $1.117$ i.i.d. origin-included series is the $1+0.109+0.008+\dots$ value.

$E\|X_i-X_j\|=E_d=[2/3+(d-1)S]/d$.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The wording is a one-to-one assignment and the 1:1 line-point normalisation is the one forced by the text.

The candidate set is the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments in the unit ball and the ensemble that is added to $\{0\}$ contains exactly $d$ points and exactly $d$ distinct segments, the numbers matching in dimension. Up to relabelling

$$X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{i},\qquad Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1)\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad i=1,\dots ,d,$$

one independent uniform point on each orthogonal arm. On this construction the simplex
${\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ is a.s. non-degenerate and

$${\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]|}{d!}
            =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|Y_{i}|}{d!},$$

so with $E|Y|=1/2$

$$E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{(1/2)^{d}}{d!}=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 .$$

No $d!/d^{d}$ deflation belongs to the model. The $d!/d^{d}$ factor is the probability that $d$ i.i.d. draws from the whole cross happen to land on $d$ different arms. Allowing collisions would put positive mass on configurations with two points on the same arm, i.e. ${\rm Vol}_{d}=0$, which is inconsistent with the requirement that the number of points and the number of distinct orthogonal segments match and that the hull be $d$-dimensional a.s.

For two different arms

$$\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\sqrt{Y_{i}^{2}+Y_{j}^{2}},\qquad
J:=E\sqrt{Y_{i}^{2}+Y_{j}^{2}}
  =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765196 .$$

Hence $E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=J$ for $i\neq j$. For the $d+1$ points $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ the mean unordered pair distance is

$$\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\,E\|X\|+\binom d2 J}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)J}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,$$

the origin-included average that the statement asks for.

The dimension-wise ratio is therefore the familiar one-point-per-arm normalisation

$$R_{d}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)2^{-d}}{d!\,[1+(d-1)J]},\qquad R_{1}=1.$$

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.0000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{3\cdot2^{-2}}{2(1+J)}\approx0.2126$,
$R_{3}= \dfrac{4\cdot2^{-3}}{6[1+2J]}\approx0.0329$,
$R_{4}= \dfrac{5\cdot2^{-4}}{24[1+3J]}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}\approx0.00038$,

$R_{d}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$. The series is exhausted after $d=4$,

$$S=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
  =1+0.2126+0.0329+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
  \approx1.2497\approx1.250$$

to three decimals. This is $1+0.212+0.033+\dots$, the $1\!:\!1$ line-point sum obtained with the distinct-arms bijection and the origin-included mean pairwise distance. The $(2d)^{-d}$ volume and the $1.117$ sum are the i.i.d. with-replacement model that allows collisions and therefore a positive probability of a degenerate hull, an extra sampling assumption not required by the distinct-segment wording.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The i.i.d. with-replacement arithmetic that is being quoted for 1.117 is internally consistent, but it is for a different sampling model than the one stated.

The candidate set is described as the union of d distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin in the unit ball and the ensemble that is added to {0} contains exactly d points and exactly d distinct segments, the numbers matching. That is a 1:1 assignment points ↔ lines, not an i.i.d. draw with replacement from the union. With the intended construction we may relabel the arms so that

X_i = U_i e_i ,  U_i ∼ U(-1,1) i.i.d., i=1…d,

one point on each orthogonal arm. On this model the d-simplex
conv{0,X_1,…,X_d} is non-degenerate a.s. and

Vol_d = |det[X_1…X_d]|/d! = ∏_{i=1}^d |U_i| / d! .

With E|U|=1/2

E Vol_d = 2^{-d}/d! ,   E Vol_1 =1/2,

the d!/d^d permutation factor that appears for sampling with replacement does not belong to the stated set-up, because replacement would allow two points on the same arm and would make the hull degenerate with positive probability, contrary to “distinct mutually orthogonal … with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”.
